description: ABOUT QUALIFYCODE AI has made it trivial to fabricate resumes, take-home assignments, and remote interviews. QualifyCode is the integrity layer for technical hiring—helping engineering teams verify candidate work objectively while keeping every hiring decision explainable, auditable, and fair. We are a small, product-focused team in Mumbai running a live production platform used in real hiring workflows. Our product spans a proctored web coding IDE, a recruiter decision console, isolated code-execution pipelines, and automated integrity and code-quality analysis services. Everything is built and owned in-house, end to end. THE ROLE We’re looking for a Software Engineer to work across the full stack rather than a single siloed layer. Our system combines event-driven workflows, service-to-service APIs, and real-time client communication—so your work will span React interfaces, TypeScript and Python backend services, PostgreSQL data models, and asynchronous job queues. At this stage of our growth, the core engineering focus is scale, reliability, and hardening—driving down end-to-end latency, optimizing database queries, refining access controls, and strengthening distributed concurrency. This role fits someone who reads how a production system actually behaves before changing it, and who ships verified fixes over quick guesses. WHAT YOU’LL OWN • Candidate Coding Experience: Build and harden our browser-based IDE—editing workflows, resilient autosave, live execution feedback over WebSockets, pre-assessment environment checks, and reliable media uploads. • Recruiter Decision Console: Develop the dashboard hiring managers rely on under time pressure—candidate reports, code-quality and integrity breakdowns, session timelines, review queues, and synchronized media playback. • Core Backend & Orchestration: Design and scale APIs and state machines handling assessment lifecycles, candidate sessions, RBAC, usage accounting, and asynchronous workflows with clean contracts and idempotent failure handling. • Analysis & Scoring Pipelines: Extend our code-quality and integrity pipelines across deterministic scoring rules, telemetry processing, computer-vision signals, and bounded LLM integrations—keeping results accurate and explainable. • Reliability & Observability: Improve resilience across execution sandboxes, PostgreSQL databases, Redis queues, and object storage. Debug issues with distributed traces and metrics, and back every fix with regression tests. OUR STACK You don't need prior fluency in every tool, but you should be strong in TypeScript and comfortable moving across frontend state, backend APIs, SQL query plans, and Python services: • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, TanStack Query, Monaco Editor, Socket.IO, browser media/WASM APIs • Backend: Node.js (NestJS, Prisma, Express), Python (FastAPI) • Data & Async: PostgreSQL, Redis, S3-compatible object storage, BullMQ, Celery, Server-Sent Events • Infra & Observability: Docker, Linux, GitHub Actions, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, k6 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR • 1–4 years of production experience shipping full-stack web applications (or equivalent demonstrated depth). • Strong TypeScript & React fundamentals—able to reason across UI state, API lifecycles, and relational schemas in the same afternoon. • Solid backend engineering: Practical grasp of HTTP semantics, auth/RBAC, idempotency, transactions, and fault-tolerant queue retries. • PostgreSQL beyond CRUD: Comfortable with joins, indexing, migrations, and reading EXPLAIN plans. • High engineering rigor: You verify changes with tests, traces, or benchmarks before calling them done. • Immediate availability to join our Mumbai office (Hybrid). Bonus points for: A live project or readable GitHub repo with real users; experience debugging distributed race conditions or retry storms; production LLM or media/computer-vision integrations; Python async services (FastAPI/Celery); or work in audited domains like HR tech or fintech. HOW WE ENGINEER • Contract-first APIs: Shared schemas, pagination standards, and permission models are strictly typed across services. • Verification by default: Bug fixes ship with regression tests; auth changes include negative (403) tests; performance work includes measurements. • Zero-downtime evolution: Database and API changes roll out via staged, backward-compatible migrations. • Safe rollouts & CI guardrails: Feature flags, shadow-mode validation for automated scoring, and automated CI checks for timeouts and bounded queries. HOW TO APPLY Please apply at https://qualifycode.com/careers (and include the following in your application or Wellfound note): 1. A working link to something you built (a live product, open-source contribution, or GitHub repo we can read). 2. One line on which part of our stack or problem space you’d most want to own.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer - 3
snippet: Homework reimagined
description: You are the engineer our customers work with directly. You take a business problem nobody has written down properly, work out what should actually be built, build it, deploy it into an environment you don't control, and stay with it until it's being used in production every day. The requirement you're given on day one is usually not the requirement that ships. Working out the difference is the job. We hire two types of engineers into this role. You need to be strong in one and credible in the other—we don't expect both at depth. Infrastructure-led. You're strong in cloud, Linux, networking, Kubernetes, and deployment automation. You've debugged a VPC routing problem and a failing Helm release in the same week. You write solid production code and can design a service end-to-end. Systems-led. You're a strong engineer—you design production systems and reason about data models, concurrency, failure modes, and APIs. You're comfortable in Linux and the cloud and have shipped through Docker and Kubernetes; you just haven't been the person who owns the cluster. Both need the same thing that isn't negotiable: you can work out what a customer actually needs when nobody has told you. Key responsibilities: Figure out what to build. Work with the customer's technical and business teams to understand the workflow the platform is meant to change. Decide what the deployment actually needs—and say no to the parts that won't move the outcome. Design for their reality. Private networks, corporate firewalls, restricted egress, existing databases, enterprise identity, data residency. Design something that works inside those constraints, not around them. Build it. Write production code—integrations, adapters, data pipelines, and deployment automation. You're in the codebase, not reviewing someone else's. Deploy and operate it. Containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, networking, observability. Own it through go-live and through the first weeks of real usage, when the interesting failures happen. Troubleshoot across every layer. An issue arises as "it's slow. " You find out whether that's the model, the query plan, the network path, or their proxy. Scope and estimate. Infrastructure sizing, BOMs, deployment plans, dependencies—and an honest account of what you can't commit to yet. Feed the field back into the product. You'll see the same gap at the third customer that you saw at the first. Turning that into a product change, sometimes by building it yourself, is part of the role. Lead a small team while staying hands-on. Two to four engineers across concurrent deployments. You stay in the code. Required qualifications & tech stack: 5+ years building and shipping production systems, with real ownership of something customers used Strong Linux fundamentals and practical networking: you can reason about DNS, routing, TLS, proxies, and firewalls when something breaks Hands-on production experience on AWS or Azure (both is a plus) Docker and Kubernetes in production—managed services (EKS / AKS / GKE) count Strong in at least one of Python, Go, or Java, and able to work in an unfamiliar one Comfortable across REST APIs, relational databases and SQL, CI/CD pipelines, and production debugging You can hold a technical conversation with a customer's architect and a difficult one with their security team You learn unfamiliar systems quickly, because every deployment contains at least one Nice-to-haves: None of these are gates. They're what makes the first few months faster. DevOps & infrastructure: Owning CI/CD end-to-end—GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, ArgoCD Observability in production: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK; building dashboards and alerts people actually act on Air-gapped or restricted-egress deployments—private registries, image mirroring, offline installs Cluster-level Kubernetes: ingress, storage classes, autoscaling, resource tuning, upgrades Secrets management (Vault, Key Vault, Secrets Manager) and certificate handling Data and services: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis Kafka, RabbitMQ, or SQS Vector stores and retrieval pipelines Enterprise and security: AD, SAML, OIDC, and SSO integration; RBAC design Security reviews, compliance frameworks, VAPT remediation Other: GCP and on-premises deployments Having built on LLMs and understanding how model behavior shapes what the product can promise Leading small teams without leaving the code

description: ### About the Role CDSPACE is looking for an Embedded Software Engineer who enjoys working close to hardware, solving challenging technical problems, and building reliable embedded systems. You will develop real-time firmware for drone gimbals, stabilization systems, avionics, and communication subsystems. The role covers the complete embedded development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, hardware bring-up, debugging, testing, optimization, and production support. ### What You’ll Do **Real-Time Firmware Development** - Develop and maintain embedded firmware using C and C++. - Build real-time firmware for drone gimbals, stabilization systems, avionics, and related subsystems. - Develop bare-metal and RTOS-based applications for STM32, ESP32, and similar microcontrollers. - Design concurrent firmware components, interrupt-driven systems, and timing-critical control functions. - Optimize firmware for execution speed, memory usage, power consumption, and reliability. **Drone Communication and Subsystem Integration** - Develop communication interfaces between flight controllers, gimbals, sensors, payloads, motor controllers, and onboard computers. - Implement and debug communication protocols such as UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, and RS-485. - Support integration with wireless communication technologies such as Bluetooth Low Energy and Wi-Fi. - Develop reliable data handling, device management, error detection, and recovery mechanisms. - Diagnose communication and integration issues across multiple embedded subsystems. **Gimbal and Motor-Control Systems** - Develop firmware for gimbal control, stabilization, sensing, and motor-drive systems. - Integrate IMUs, encoders, motor drivers, and other motion-control sensors. - Work with BLDC motors, motor controllers, and electronic speed controllers. - Support the implementation and tuning of control algorithms for stabilization and motor control. - Diagnose timing, vibration, sensor, communication, and control-related issues. **Hardware Bring-Up and Device Drivers** - Develop and maintain board support packages, hardware-abstraction layers, and device drivers. - Bring up new microcontroller-based boards and validate clocks, memory, power sequencing, peripherals, and communication interfaces. - Port firmware to new hardware platforms and microcontroller variants. - Read electronic schematics and component datasheets to support firmware development and debugging. - Collaborate with hardware engineers to diagnose board-level and hardware-software integration issues. **Bootloaders and Firmware Updates** - Develop and maintain bootloaders and firmware-update mechanisms. - Support wired and wireless firmware-update workflows. - Implement firmware validation, rollback, recovery, and fail-safe mechanisms. - Improve the reliability and usability of production programming and update processes. **Debugging, Testing, and Validation** - Debug firmware using hardware debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and other laboratory instruments. - Develop unit, integration, hardware-in-the-loop, and system-level tests. - Investigate firmware defects, timing issues, memory corruption, communication failures, and hardware faults. - Perform root-cause analysis and implement corrective actions. - Support bench testing, field testing, flight trials, and production validation. - Maintain test procedures, debugging records, and technical documentation. **Production and Engineering Support** - Improve firmware build, programming, calibration, and production-test workflows. - Support manufacturing teams during board programming, testing, and failure analysis. - Use Git for version control, collaboration, code review, and release management. - Work with hardware, avionics, controls, and flight-test teams to resolve system-level issues. - Maintain clear documentation for firmware architecture, interfaces, configuration, and releases. ### Required Qualifications and Skills - Strong hands-on experience with Embedded C/C++ and low-level programming. - Experience with bare-metal development and microcontrollers such as STM32, ESP32, or similar platforms. - Understanding of microcontroller peripherals, interrupts, timers, ADCs, DMA, memory, and watchdogs. - Experience with UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, RS-485, and related embedded communication protocols. - Understanding of RTOS concepts, task scheduling, synchronization, concurrency, and inter-process communication. - Experience developing device drivers, board support packages, and hardware-abstraction layers. - Knowledge of bootloader development and firmware-update mechanisms. - Strong firmware debugging and root-cause analysis skills. - Experience using hardware debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and other laboratory instruments. - Ability to read electronic schematics, component datasheets, and technical documentation. - Basic hardware fault-finding and board bring-up skills. - Familiarity with Git and software version-control practices. - Ability to communicate technical findings clearly and work effectively across engineering teams. ### Good to Have - Experience with drones, UAV avionics, autopilots, or gimbal systems. - Knowledge of BLDC motors, motor drivers, electronic speed controllers, and motor-control techniques. - Experience integrating IMUs, encoders, cameras, or other UAV sensors and payloads. - Experience with Bluetooth Low Energy, Wi-Fi, or other wireless communication technologies. - Familiarity with control systems, sensor fusion, and stabilization algorithms. - Experience with PX4, ArduPilot, MAVLink, or similar UAV technologies. - Exposure to FPGA development and FPGA-microcontroller integration. - Experience taking embedded products from prototype through manufacturing and production. **Experience:** 2+ years in embedded software or firmware development. **Education:** B.E./B.Tech in Electronics and Communication, Electrical and Electronics, Instrumentation, Computer Science, or a related field.

You are someone who enjoys identifying weaknesses, designing preventative controls, and building security automation that scales with the platform. Responsibilities: Identify and secure attack surfaces across our AWS infrastructure, Kubernetes clusters, and internal platforms by proactively assessing misconfigurations, access risks, and exposed services. Design and implement preventative cloud security guardrails, including IAM hardening, network controls, secrets management, and infrastructure security best practices. Conduct security design reviews for new services and infrastructure changes to identify architectural risks before systems reach production. Build and integrate security checks directly into CI/CD pipelines to enforce automated scanning for vulnerabilities, container images, infrastructure configurations, and application dependencies. Develop automation and internal tooling to detect, prevent, and remediate security issues such as leaked secrets, excessive permissions, insecure configurations, and vulnerable dependencies. Perform threat modeling and adversarial analysis of infrastructure and application systems to identify realistic attack paths and improve system defenses. Improve visibility into the security posture of our systems through monitoring, logging, and security signal generation across cloud infrastructure and workloads. Investigate security incidents and vulnerabilities, perform root cause analysis, and implement long-term fixes to prevent recurrence. Collaborate closely with platform, infrastructure, and application engineering teams to ensure security is embedded in development workflows and infrastructure design. Contribute to building scalable security practices, including vulnerability management processes, security automation frameworks, and infrastructure security standards. Requirements: 4-8 years of experience in cloud security, DevSecOps, security engineering, or related roles involving infrastructure and application security. Strong understanding of applied cryptography and ability to choose the right security tools, techniques, and approach for securing systems from a variety of threats. Strong hands-on experience securing AWS environments, including IAM policies, networking controls, access management, logging, and infrastructure hardening. Practical experience working with Kubernetes and containerized environments, including securing container images, workloads, and cluster configurations. Experience integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines and development workflows, including automated vulnerability scanning and dependency security checks. Ability to write automation and security tooling using scripting or programming languages such as Python, Go, or similar. Familiarity with Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform and an understanding of securing infrastructure configurations and deployment pipelines. Experience identifying and remediating cloud security risks such as excessive IAM permissions, exposed services, insecure secrets management, and vulnerable infrastructure components. Understanding of common cloud and application security threats, including privilege escalation, credential leakage, network exposure, and supply chain vulnerabilities. Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to think adversarially about systems and proactively identify potential attack paths. Excellent collaboration and communication skills (verbal as well as written) with the ability to work closely with engineering teams and other stakeholders to improve security posture without slowing development velocity. Bonus experience includes security research, penetration testing, bug bounty participation, building internal security tooling, or contributions to security-focused open-source projects. It does not build the things no single pod owns: * the customer and entity model every product reads from * the document pipeline every filing runs through * the integration layer that pulls in accounting data * permissions and access control * the AI infrastructure the pods build on Left to the pods, those get built four different ways, or once and then never touched again. Core Product owns that layer. Part of the job is deciding what belongs in the core layer, which means telling a pod no when they want a special case. ### Surge capacity Once or twice a quarter a project matters enough to the company that it outgrows the pod carrying it.
